newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Analysts divided over prospects of Sweden rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Analysts divided over prospects of Sweden rate cut.

text.p: The Swedish central bank, the Riksbank, may cut its key repurchase rate as early as Tuesday, but is more likely to wait until mid-December, according to analysts polled by Reuters on Monday.
The bank will issue its own report on inflation and inflationary expectations on December 17.
But a minority, seven out of 16 analysts polled, said the Riksbank might take the bold step of lowering the rate as early as Tuesday.
"I think the cut will come together with the inflation report," said Bjorn Englund, economist at Unibors Markets.
"Fundamentals certainly speak for a cut now but the Riksbank has said we should not focus on the first repurchase operation after the four that expire," he said.
Those who anticipate a cut say on average it will be 15 basis points from the current rate of 4.60 percent. Their forecasts ranged from five to 25 basis points.
"There have been good economic data and there is room for a cut. If you're going to do it at all, why not straight away," said Tomas Niemela, economist at Aragon brokerage.

The Riksbank has cut the repo rate by 431 basis points since January. The last, a 0.25 percentage point cut, was on October 24, when the Riksbank also reduced deposit and lending rates 50 basis points each to 4.25 and 5.75 percent respectively.
At the time the central bank said there was some room for further cuts but that indicators did not all point in the same direction.
"That means more time is needed to collate and analyse incoming information. The conclusion could be to leave the repo rate unchanged," Riksbank governor Urban Backstrom said in October.
Deputy bank governor Lars Heikensten adopted the same formula when he commented on consumer price data for October which showed year-on-year deflation for the first time since 1959.

Aragon, Consensus, Den Danske Bank, Deutsche/Morgan Grenfell, Freningsbanken, Handelsbanken, Lehman Brothers, Morgan Stanley, Nomura, Nordbanken, PaineWebber, Salomon Brothers, S-E-Banken, Sparbanken, UBS och Unibank Markets.
